newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES DRIFT ON FX, SHORT-TERM RATE JITTERS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES DRIFT ON FX, SHORT-TERM RATE JITTERS.

text.p: Greek stocks continued to drift lower in early Thursday deals but this time the decline was broadly-based and analysts said equity prices fell in response to forex outflows and higher short-term depo rates.
"The market has been spooked by the turmoil in the forex market and soaring short-term rates," said Takis Niarhos, analyst at Hellenic-American Securities.
"Buying interest remains satisfactory, absorbing much of the supply but the market may slide down to 1,500 points until the money and fx markets return to normalcy."
Telesis Securities endorsed the same view in its daily report.
"Although Wednesday's upheaval in the money market is unlikely to continue for long, it weighs negatively on sentiment," it said.
Dollar/drachma was quoted around one drachma higher than Wednesday' 281.5 Bank of Greece fixing.
The central bank intervened on Wednesday in the forex market selling 660 million ecus and $60 million to prop up the domestic currency, dealers said.
Depo rates were holding Wednesday's high levels in early Thursday deals. The one-month Athibor, Greece's reference rate, had firmed 39 basis points to 11.97 percent on Wednesday.
Long-term bonds and FRNs were flat but vulnerable to higher interbank rates and forex developments.
Market participants said prospects remained favourable in the medium-term but the market was in need of fresh positive impetus.
"We have yet to enter the peak of the interim results announcement period and equities have not started to respond to accelerating 1997 profitability," said Niarhos.
Telesis Securities also saw the absence of news pushing stocks lower in the short-term.
"The absence of major stock market moving news strengthens the possibility of a short-term weakness but significant downside risk is limited," it said.
The Athens general index was off 1.11 percent or 17.46 points to 1,555.41 from Wednesday's 1,572.87 close after 25 minutes of trading.
Turnover amounted to 1.8 billion drachmas on volume of 0.7 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 84 to 29 with 23 shares unchanged on 136 traded.
OTE telecom OTEq.L Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.875-$11.20. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,113-1,143 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,042-1,102 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock were down 45 drachmas to 6,215.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 614.58-653.81 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $70.98-$73.75. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,313-3,532 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.86-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 222-253 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 **** Users
